definition_and_proof_review.only_changes_relative_to_v3_mathematics_: Two intended clarification insertions: versioned binary grader predicate and its freely selectable-candidate conditional reward. Reverting these restores v3 mathematical text.
definition_and_proof_review.binary_predicate: C_t = g_d(A_t,Y*) in {0,1}; exact equality is a special case. The existing reward reduction, transition decomposition and Snell/persistence arguments use only binary correctness and retain their stated assumptions.
definition_and_proof_review.candidate_reward: max over available a of E[g_d(a,Y*) | F_t] is the binary-grader analogue of the exact-answer immediate correctness reward. It is distinct from claiming that the actual fitted selector/controller attains it.
definition_and_proof_review.proof_findings: No material mathematical discrepancy identified. The true conditional drift, conditional-versus-feature information, finite-horizon optimum, fixed-process stake ordering, persistence assumptions and sequential coverage scope are preserved.

figure5.finding: Offline reference labels feed fitting/evaluation; frozen parameters and current/past observations feed runtime decisions. Continuation adds a response/cost. The caption limits the diagram to the information contract and does not assert a fitted Bellman optimum or executed peer fleet.

figure6.caption: Delayed repair defeats a myopic stopping rule.
figure6.finding: All node, edge, stop and forced-horizon values match the source. The caption explicitly distinguishes the abstract floor0 from live floor2 and states that this is not new generated evidence.
